title: Walk to School Week
intro: Text 1 is a poster from a student council about a week of walking to school.

visual.text: The best ten minutes of your day are not in a car.
Walk to School Week — leave the back seat and use your feet.
Four students in uniform stroll along a covered walkway, laughing and sharing a packet of biscuits. Behind them, a long line of cars waits outside the school gate.

Every morning, the road outside our gate fills with cars, and those of us in the back seats arrive sleepy and silent. For one week, try something different. Get off the bus a stop early, or ask to be dropped at the park. Walk the rest with a friend. You will reach class awake, with a story to tell.

visual.title: How it works
items: Collect a stamp card from your form teacher
Walk in on any morning and have it stamped at the gate before 7.20 am
Five stamps earn you a breakfast set from the canteen
The class with the most stamps chooses the music at Friday’s assembly

visual.text: “I used to scroll on my phone all the way to school. Now I walk with my neighbour, and we have actually become friends.” — Hui Min, Secondary 3
Live too far away to walk? Join a Walking Bus from Block 204 or the MRT station, led by prefects, at 6.55 am.
Pick up your stamp card on Monday

text2.intro: Text 2 is taken from a letter a parent wrote to the school newsletter after the walking week.
paragraphs: For three years I drove my daughter right up to the school gate. Every morning she slept against the window while I fought the traffic, and neither of us said a word. During the walking week, she asked me to drop her at the park instead. I was worried she would be late. She was not.

On the Wednesday she came home full of news: the old man who feeds the mynahs by the canal, a shortcut her friend had found behind the market, and a bet about whose umbrella would break first. That evening she talked more at dinner than she had in a month. The week is over, but we have kept the park drop-off. I lose ten minutes of driving; I gain a daughter who arrives at school awake.

questions.text: Look at Text 1. Which sentence sums up what the poster most wants students to believe?

options.label: A
options.text: Students should stop being driven to school because cars pollute the air.

options.label: B
options.text: Walking even part of the way makes the school morning livelier and friendlier.

options.label: C
options.text: Students who walk to school can win a free breakfast from the canteen.

scheme.answer: Walking even part of the way makes the school morning livelier and friendlier.

questions.text: Look at the picture in Text 1. How does it support the headline ‘The best ten minutes of your day are not in a car.’?

scheme.answer: The students walking are laughing and sharing biscuits while the cars sit in a queue behind them, so walking looks far more enjoyable than being in a car.
accept: It contrasts the happy walkers in front with the cars stuck at the gate, showing the walk is the better part of the morning.

seeds.text: The students are laughing and sharing biscuits as they walk, while behind them the cars are stuck in a long line, so walking looks like the best part of the day and being in a car does not.
The walkers are having fun together but the cars are jammed at the gate, so it shows walking is more enjoyable than sitting in a car.
It shows that cars are dangerous for students crossing the road.
It shows some students walking to school.
Four students in uniform stroll along a covered walkway.
